newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on Argentine crop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply higher on Argentine crop.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended sharply higher, nearly erasing Friday's limit losses amid reports Argentina's soybean production could fall and on strong USDA weekly export inspections, traders said.

Floor sources said rumors circulated that a leading analytical firm had cut its estimates for Argentine soybean production. The U.S. agricultural attache also cut Argentina's output to 13.25 million tonnes, down 0.25 million.
Soybeans opened quietly higher on the Argentine reports but surged near midsession after USDA put weekly export inspections at 13.8 million bushels.

While the figure was not surprising, it suggested the export pace was outstripping USDA's expectations. Analysts said export inspections needed to drop below 10 million bushels per week to meet USDA's target of 900 million bushels.

The strong export figure lent support to arguments USDA would have to cut its ending stocks projection from 140 million bushels in Friday's report. Soybeans tumbled on Friday partly due to ideas USDA would keep the stocks unchanged.
Soybeans ended 21-3/4 to 3-1/2 cents higher, with May up 21-3/4 at $8.62-3/4 a bushel and new crop November up 11 cents at $7.05.

Gains were limited by speculation a cold, wet spring in the U.S. Midwest would force farmers to switch intended corn acreage to soybeans. Soybeans can be planted as late as July while corn must be in the ground by June.

Funds were active buyers on the day after leading Friday's sell-off, floor sources said. Traders said Prudential Securities bought two million bushels May and one million July, Refco Inc bought 1.5 million May and Cargill Investor Services bought two million July and sold two million July, traders said.
The July/November spread tacked on 9-1/2 cents per bushel, premium July and closed at $1.62-1/2, premium July.
Cargill Inc spread 2.5 million bushels November/July at $1.60 to $1.61, premium July and Continental Grain spread 1.5 million bushels May/July at five cents, premium July.

In options trade, Produce Grain bought 200 May $8.50 puts and sold 200 May $8.25 puts at 11-1/2 to 12 cents, traders said. Tradelink bought 250 July $8.50 calls and sold 500 May $8.75 calls at 28 cents.
Soybean volume was estimated by CBOT at 75,000 contracts, compared with Friday's actual volume of 93,876 contracts.
